newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan gives nod to foreigners' property projects.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan gives nod to foreigners' property projects.

text.p: The Interior Ministry has acted to open Taiwan's property market, saying on Tuesday it had approved three applications by foreign interests to invest more than T$40 billion in Taiwan real estate developments.
They were the first such approvals since Taiwan liberalised its investment rules in May by lifting a ban on foreigners buying, selling and renting real estate properties.
Such investments now are permitted on a case-by-case basis.
Of the three cases, Hong Kong-funded Hung Tu Development Corp was allowed to invest T$38 billion in an industrial zone on reclaimed land in Yulin, officials said.
The company planned to develop the area as a chemical, metal and machinery and consumer zone.

Another Hong Kong property firm planned to invest T$1.8 billion to build a recreation centre and apartments in southern Kaohsiung, while a Taiwan-Canada joint venture would pour T$200 million into a new commercial building in Taipei.
The investments need final approval from the Economic Ministry's Investment Commission, officials said.
